pull_request.title: fix(vitruvian-tool-github): a row's id is a name the app will read
pull_request.body:
**Found on screen.** Installing the GitHub tool 1.0.0 from the catalogue into the released app (3.46.0): the hand-off worked and the tool's Settings panel said "Connected as @ipv1337", but its island page was a spinner for ever. The tool's log: `a page for the panel status was not drawn: blocks[0].id is not well formed`.

**Cause.** The rows were named `repo:owner/name` and `pr:owner/name#12`. The protocol reads an id only as letters, digits, hyphen and underscore in parts joined by dots, and the app, correctly, draws none of a page with one id that is not.

**Fix.** An owner and a name are written with `_` as `__` and `.` as `_d`, in parts joined by dots: `repo.acme.web`, `pr.acme.web.12`. That reads back exactly whatever the repository is called (`.github`, `a.b`, `a__d`); a name too long for an id gets a short stand-in, so it keeps its row and never costs the page.

**Why no test caught it, and what does now.** The page tests held the ids as text, and the conformance run is signed out, so no test read a signed-in page the way the app does. `testEveryPageIsOneTheAppWillRead` sends every page through the protocol's own reader; `testARowsIdIsAWellFormedNameWhateverTheRepositoryIsCalled` holds ten awkward names to the protocol's rule and to reading back. Both failed before the fix.

**Proven live.** With the fixed program in the installed tool, the island page draws the watched repository's checks and the open pull requests.

Cuts tool 1.0.1; the catalogue entry follows with its size and checksum.
